holidays.name: National Clam Chowder Day
holidays.description: A day to grab a spoon and settle the great chowder debate: creamy New England, tomato-based Manhattan, or one of the other regional versions. Slurp a bowl, preferably with oyster crackers on the side.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance held every February 25. The dish itself comes from coastal fishing communities, where clams were easy to harvest and made a cheap, filling stew.
holidays.funFact: Manhattan clam chowder likely came from Portuguese fishing communities in Rhode Island, who were known for tomato-based stews. The name is probably a nod to the tomato broth and the New York fish market where they sold their catch.

holidays.name: National Chocolate Covered Nuts Day
holidays.description: A day for snacking on nuts dipped in chocolate. Almonds, peanuts, hazelnuts and cashews all count, and the sweet-and-salty crunch makes it an easy holiday to celebrate.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial snack observance of unclear origin, held on February 25 each year.
holidays.funFact: It falls in February, which is also Celebration of Chocolate Month, so the holiday comes with built-in company.

holidays.name: National Pistol Patent Day
holidays.description: A day marking the moment a Connecticut inventor won the patent for a practical revolving-chamber pistol. It's a history-and-technology observance that looks back at the invention that reshaped firearms manufacturing.
holidays.origin: On February 25, 1836, Samuel Colt received his first U.S. patent for a percussion-cap pistol with a revolving chamber that could fire several shots without reloading.
holidays.funFact: Colt wasn't the first to try the revolving-firearm idea, but he was the first to turn it into a practical design. His patent helped make Connecticut a manufacturing powerhouse.
